statement: For any finite deterministic positive-weight layered path family visiting exactly one site of each layer t, with independent N(0,sigma_t^2) site weights and m_t sites in layer t, F=log(sum_p a_p exp(beta sum_t omega[t,p_t])) satisfies Var(F)=beta^2 sum_t sigma_t^2/m_t+Var(F(R)), where R[t,x]=omega[t,x]-m_t^{-1}sum_y omega[t,y].
assumptions: Finite nonempty path family; deterministic positive path weights
Every path visits exactly one site per layer
Independent Gaussian site variables, constant variance within a layer
Fixed finite beta; deterministic normalization allowed

source.ranking_context: RANKING_2026-09-07.csv:544: C0120; attempted_un; power improvement of polymer variance (KPZ)

proof: Each layer mean A_t has variance sigma_t^2/m_t and is independent of its centered Gaussian residual vector. Different layers are independent. Every path has the same additive beta sum_t A_t, so F(omega)=beta sum_t A_t+F(R). Independence gives the identity. Finite log-sum-exp is square integrable by its linear-growth bound.
remaining_gap: No upper bound on Var(F(R)); this finite-temperature identity is an auxiliary result, while the recovered primary target is the ground-state maximum. No parent-problem solution is claimed.

statement: For a finite deterministic nonempty layered path family visiting exactly one site in each layer, with m_t independent unit Gaussian sites in layer t, M=max_p sum_t g[t,p_t] satisfies Var(M)=sum_t 1/m_t+Var(M(R)). In the unrestricted source model this implies Var(M_n)>=H_n. If every m_t<=W, then Var(M)>=N/W for N layers.
assumptions: Finite deterministic path family and layer sets
Every path visits one site in every layer
proof: Subtract each independent Gaussian layer average A_t. Every path receives the same sum A_t; M(g)=sum A_t+M(R). Independence and square integrability give exact variance addition. Source layer t has t+1 sites, t=0,...,n-1.
remaining_gap: No power upper bound on the residual maximum's variance; cannot transfer a strip variance bound to the unrestricted family by monotonicity.

statement: For all r>=1, iid standard Gaussian vertex weights and all up/right paths from (0,0) to (r,r) restricted to |x-y|<=1, counting N=2r+1 vertices, the ground-state maximum has expectation r/sqrt(pi) and variance (2-1/pi)r+1. Thus its variance per visited vertex tends to 1-1/(2pi).
assumptions: Fixed endpoint (r,r) and width-one diagonal strip
iid N(0,1) vertex weights, including both endpoints
proof: Every path uses r+1 diagonal junctions and one of two disjoint intermediate vertices in each of r diamonds. M=sum G_k+sum max(X_k,Y_k), all summands independent. For iid X,Y, max=(X+Y)/2+|(X-Y)/2| and the two Gaussian terms are independent. Var(max)=1-1/pi. Add r+1 junction variances.
remaining_gap: The original target has unrestricted paths and a free endpoint. No variance comparison allows this restricted example to decide it.

statement: In the width-one strip of L2, under OU noise g^s=e^(-s)g+sqrt(1-e^(-2s))g', q(s)=arccos(e^(-s))/pi and the number B of different diamond choices has law Binomial(r,q(s)). Identical-path probability is (1-q)^r and expected normalized common-vertex overlap is 1-rq/(2r+1). For s=r^(-alpha), 0<alpha<2, identical-path probability tends to zero while normalized overlap tends to one and variance stays linear. This refutes the auxiliary implication from high-probability maximizer change alone to power variance improvement.
assumptions: Independent Gaussian copy g' at all vertices
Fixed alpha in (0,2) for the asymptotic assertion
No extra O(N/log N) variance premise is asserted for this counterexample
proof: Each diamond choice is the sign of an independent Gaussian difference. Original and OU differences have correlation e^(-s); planar Gaussian angle gives sign mismatch arccos(e^(-s))/pi. Disjoint diamond environments prove independence. All r+1 junctions coincide; a mismatching diamond loses exactly one shared vertex. q(s)~sqrt(2s)/pi proves the limits.
remaining_gap: Does not refute C0120 or the correctly quantified overlap-chaos route. Need polynomial overlap bounds in the unrestricted model.
